title: Admin Directory: Replace Photo column images with clickable filenames and modal preview (no other UI changes)

requirements.text: Update ONLY the Administrative Directory Table Photo column header cell at XPath `/html[1]/body[1]/div[1]/div[1]/main[1]/div[1]/div[4]/div[1]/div[3]/div[2]/div[1]/div[1]/table[1]/thead[1]/tr[1]/th[4]` so that its user-facing label remains unchanged (e.g., still shows the same "Photo" text) and no other table header styling/structure changes occur.

quotes:
Use the XPath expressions to identify the elements to edit.
The user instructions should be applied ONLY to the elements selected in this prompt.

acceptanceCriteria: The table header cell at the specified XPath displays the exact same label as before (no wording, casing, spacing, alignment, size, padding, or icon changes).
No other `<th>` elements in the table are changed.

requirements.text: Update ONLY the Administrative Directory Table Photo column body cell at XPath `/html[1]/body[1]/div[1]/div[1]/main[1]/div[1]/div[4]/div[1]/div[3]/div[2]/div[1]/div[1]/table[1]/tbody[1]/tr[1]/td[4]` so that it no longer renders an `` (or any image element) inline. Instead, render the photo *filename as text only* (derived from the representative photo path), styled as a clickable link/button. Clicking the filename must open an overlay/modal showing the full-size image.

quotes:
1. Replace the actual image display in the 'Photo column' with the photo file name (text only).
2.  Make the photo name clickable.
3. On click, open the full-size image in an overlay/modal window.

Please update only the Photo column behavior in the Administrative Directory Table.

 Strict warning - Ensure that no other UI elements or functionality in the Administrative Directory table are affected, any UI changes are not acceptable.

acceptanceCriteria: The Photo column cell at the specified XPath does not load/render any images until the user clicks the filename.
The Photo column cell displays a filename (text) corresponding to the stored photo path (e.g., last path segment after `/`).
Clicking the filename opens a modal/overlay containing the full-size image loaded from the existing photo path resolution logic.
Closing the modal/overlay (via close button and/or clicking the backdrop) returns the user to the table with no row/table state changes.
No other `<td>` elements, columns, row layout, sorting/filtering controls, or table behavior are changed.

requirements.text: Ensure the new Photo modal/overlay behavior is performance-safe: the full-size image request must be initiated only when the user clicks a filename, not during initial table render, and the modal must not trigger any additional directory refetches or mutations.

quotes: Now that the number of leaders has increased, all images attempt to load simultaneously, which is causing noticeable page lag and performance issues.

acceptanceCriteria: On initial render of the Administrative Directory Table, the browser network log shows no image requests originating from the Photo column cells.
Clicking a filename triggers exactly one image load for that clicked item (no preloading of other rows’ images).
Opening/closing the modal does not trigger directory data refetching or change any non-Photo UI state (expanded rows, filters, search, pagination if present).

constraints: Apply changes ONLY to the two selected elements identified by the provided XPaths (Photo column header th[4] and Photo column cell td[4]) within the Administrative Directory Table.
Do not introduce any UI changes to other table columns, headers, rows, spacing, typography, icons, controls, or behavior; any non-Photo-column UI changes are unacceptable.
Use English for any user-facing text.
Do not modify files under `frontend/src/components/ui` or other paths listed in `frontend.immutablePaths`.
Backend is single-actor; no backend changes are required for this request unless strictly necessary.
nonGoals: Adding new table features (sorting, filtering, pagination changes).
Changing directory data schema or photo storage format.
Adding image thumbnails, placeholders, or lazy-loading inline images in the Photo column (the Photo column must be text-only until click).
Changing styling/theme of the Admin Dashboard or the table beyond what is strictly necessary inside the Photo column elements.
